findings.where: Screen 2 text and the tray label 'Turns'
findings.what: "A circle is a machine that turns" is absolute and wrong for the gauge circle Dan meets on screens 10, 12 and 13; say "A large circle is usually a machine that turns", as the explain already does.

The switch panel is hidden until a right answer and then appears at once above the drawing (up to two rows, about 150 px on screens 3 and 7), so the picture and the feedback jump down just as the answer's motion plays; reserve its space or fade it in.
The words teach the filter, cylinder and tank but not the cooler, accumulator or gauge, so those three can only be matched by elimination or trial; one more sentence fits (the screen is at 42 words).
A gauge's pointer looks like the adjusting arrow and the lesson never says how to tell them apart (the pointer stays inside a small circle, the adjusting arrow crosses the whole part).
"Tap Fill" and "Tap Arrow" name the group labels, which are not buttons; say "Tap Empty" and "Tap On".

findings.where: Screen 8, the say under the kit
findings.what: The words that fade in repeat screen 2's pump reading before they reach the cutaway, which brings the screen to about 89 words (99 after a Turn); lead the say with the cutaway sentence and drop the repeat on this screen.
"1 of 6 are matched" should read "1 of 6 is matched".

findings.where: Screens 1 and 10 at 360 px, SVG labels
findings.what: Labels drawn at 12 to 13 px in the 340-unit drawing render at about 10.4 to 11.3 px on a phone (the teal card names such as "Tank" about 10 px), under the 12 px the lesson's own description promises; enlarge them.

The jack and its 2000 N fade out and a pump named "Hydraulic pump, fixed" fades in with no sentence linking the two, a screen before that name is taught; add one bridging sentence to the right-answer feedback, or keep the jack.
"In a motor the tail does" uses a different word from screen 3's "its flat side does", and a triangle has no obvious tail; use "flat side" in both.

findings.where: Screen 3 Why and the kit's say for a motor
findings.what: "Oil flowing in turns the circle" makes the drawing turn; say it turns the shaft, as the explain does.
"Most symbols mean the same however they are turned" never names the exception the brief promised (a tank and the lines into it stay as drawn); name it in one sentence.
The ports carry no In and Out marks, so the say's "carry oil round the outside" has no direction to read against the symbol's lines; add small In and Out labels.
The brief listed a single-acting cylinder among the parts, but only the double-acting one appears.
